name: read-each-of-nine-spotlight-textures-through-one-dynamic-array-index
rationale:
Nine `texture2d<float, read>` handles are stored into a `metal::array<metal::array<texture2d, 3>, 3>` alloca and read back through a DYNAMIC pair of indices, so the translator cannot name the image: Logical SPIR-V has no pointer-to-image, and the emitter has to replay the whole store set as a select tree over the nine ids and prove every arm is available at the read. That is the only thing this case is for -- it is the smallest of the two hosts for the direct-image replay path, and no authored case reached it.

All nine arms are live in one dispatch. `systemSize` is 9 and `polynomialCount` is 1, so the guard admits global simdgroup indices 0..8; the dispatch is nine threadgroups of thirty-two threads, one simdgroup each, so that index IS the threadgroup id. `spotlightCount` is (3, 3) and the weight-plane array has one slice, so the tile coordinate is (g / 3, g % 3) and the selected handle is `array[g % 3][g / 3]` -- a transpose of the pair, which is why the nine indices are a permutation and not the identity, and why swapping the two selector lanes is visible rather than silent.

Each spotlight texture is 2x2 and carries its own decade plus a per-texel unit: texture t holds 10*(t+1) + 2*y + x. So the answer names both the texture that was read AND the texels that were read from it. The three tile sizes differ -- a 3x3 image cut into 3x3 tiles gives per-axis extents 2, 2, 1 -- so the nine sums cover four, four, two, two and one texel and no two of the nine results collide.

Everything else is authored to fold to exactly one so the comparison can be exact. `modulationMaskStrength` is 0, which makes the mask term 1 whatever the mask holds; `applyDifferenceModulation` is 0, which selects 1 over the whole sqrt/exp/reciprocal chain, so `air.fast_sqrt` and `air.fast_exp` still execute but their results are discarded by an OpSelect and cannot move the answer; the weight plane is 1 and the poly target is (1, 2, 4), which spreads one scalar across three distinguishable lanes so a component mix-up is visible. `systemSize` is neither 1 nor the array length, so the two reassociating selects both take their default arm and the accumulated term is the selected texel times (1, 2, 4).

Exactness: every spotlight value is a small integer, so the per-lane products, the `air.simd_sum.v3f32` across thirty-two lanes and the `endLambda` bias of 100 are all integers below 2^24 and float32 holds every partial sum exactly, in any order the reduction picks. The largest result is 924. The output buffer is thirty-two floats and only twenty-seven may be written; the tail holds -1, which no arm can produce because every result is at least 146.

execution_safety is authored_bounded: the accumulation loop steps the lane index by `threads_per_simdgroup` and exits once it reaches the tile's texel count, which the authored 3x3 image and 3x3 tile grid bound at 4. With thirty-two lanes every active lane runs exactly one iteration and lanes past the texel count run none. The store loop that follows is a literal three iterations.

name: linked-single-unit-average-tmp-input
rationale: Every source, destination, kernel, stride, dilation, threadgroup cube, and group-count extent is exactly one with zero offsets. name: downsample-a-signed-rgb-tile-under-an-unsigned-alpha
rationale:
data_type=1 selects the signed-char instantiation, whose 5x5 alpha-weighted downsample is the only corpus caller of air.convert.f.v3f32.s.v3i8 -- and it reads the SAME four bytes two ways: RGB through the signed converter and alpha through air.convert.f.f32.u.i8, unsigned. A byte of 0xC4 therefore weighs -60 into the colour sum and a byte of 0xD2 weighs +210 into the alpha sum, so a lowering that got the signedness of either one wrong could not produce this output.
The 8x8 source and 4x4 destination put every one of the 16 outputs on a different clipped footprint of the 25-tap kernel, from 9 taps at the corners to all 25 in the middle, which exercises the two bounds guards as well as the conversion.
Robustness: both conversions out of float truncate, so the case is sound as long as no component lands near an integer. Every source RGB is held to +/-60 and every alpha to 200..255, which bounds every colour quotient by 60*255/200 = 76.5 and keeps it inside signed char by construction rather than by luck; the pattern was then searched for the largest minimum distance to an integer boundary, 0.0047, about two thousand ulp at this magnitude. The pattern was also required to give the same 64 truncated bytes when the fdiv is modelled as a reciprocal multiply, so the one genuinely knife-edge component -- alpha, which is structurally acc.w*255/acc.w and therefore exactly 255 -- was checked under both divide models before the case was authored.

name: global-ushort-built-ins-in-a-20x3-grid-of-16x2-threadgroups

The AIR has no loop.

name: manual-half4-fetch-at-an-offset-transformed-onto-three-of-four-pixels
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's manual-vertex-fetch case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero constants gave a degenerate position. Constant 132 enables manual fetch; table slot 0 holds the same-library callback re::vertexfetch::fetchFromHalf4, and record 0 of the vertex-argument buffer (15 records of 24 bytes, the rest null) points at half4 positions with stride 8 and offset 8, which skips a leading decoy vertex (40, 40, 40). The three positions are (-1, -1), (3, -1), (-1, 3) with z = 1/4 with the matrix z scale 2, so world z = 5/8. The instance matrix (objectToCrWorld, column-major) scales x and y by 1/2, scales z and translates by (-1/4, -1/4, 1/8); crWorldToProjArray[0] keeps x, y and w and maps z to z/2 + 1/16, so the clip triangle is (-3/4, -3/4), (5/4, -3/4), (-3/4, 5/4) at w = 1. It covers the pixel centres (-1/2, 1/2), (-1/2, -1/2) and (1/2, -1/2) of the 2x2 target with a margin of at least 1/4 from every edge and misses (1/2, 1/2): pixel (1, 0) keeps its fill. The depth is the same at all three vertices, so its interpolation is exact; every product and sum is a small dyadic value, exact in float with or without contraction, and the observer writes (x + 1/2, y + 1/2, z, 1) for each covered pixel. screenSpaceDepthBias = 1/4 adds 1/4 * w to clip z: depth 0.625.

name: manual-vertex-fetch-null-buffer-defaults

name: a-byte-copy-whose-tail-is-shorter-than-its-vector
rationale: fastGPUMemcpyKernel copies a byte count that is not a multiple of its 16-byte vector step: every thread copies one aligned <4 x i32> chunk, and thread 0 additionally copies the len%16 trailing bytes with a DYNAMIC-length llvm.memcpy. 37 bytes is two whole chunks plus a five-byte tail, so the case separates the vector body from the tail: a translation that keeps only the chunk copy still writes 32 correct bytes and leaves bytes 32..36 at their fill value. The destination is 64 bytes and only 37 are copied, so the untouched tail of the buffer also pins that nothing is over-copied. The AIR CFG is acyclic; the only loop is the one this translator introduces for the dynamic-length copy, and the authored length of 37 bounds it at five iterations.

name: shift-a-whole-simd-cluster-out-through-the-fill
rationale:
**This case MISMATCHES on purpose: it is the reproducer for an open bug, and the fix is not in this commit.** Columns 2 and 4 come back as `data` from the lane's own position where Metal answers `filling_data`.

`simd_shuffle_and_fill_up` and `simd_shuffle_and_fill_down` are the same definition in opposite directions: within each `modulo`-wide cluster lane `l` reads `data[l -+ delta]`, and a lane whose source leaves the cluster reads `filling_data` at the wrapped position. At `delta == modulo` every lane's source leaves the cluster, so every lane must answer `filling_data` at its own position. `lower_simd_shuffle_and_fill_up` reduces `delta` modulo the cluster width BEFORE comparing it against the lane, so at `delta == modulo` it compares against zero, finds every lane in bounds and answers `data`; `lower_simd_shuffle_and_fill_down` does not reduce and answers `filling_data`. The two mirror lowerings cannot both be right, which is what pointed at this.

`delta == modulo` is not an exotic input. The two-argument overload passes `modulo = __metal_get_simdgroup_size()`, so `simd_shuffle_and_fill_up(data, fill, 32)` on a 32-wide simdgroup spells exactly it. Corpus reach is 0 by static census -- none of the 500 `simd_shuffle_and_fill_*` call sites in the 14579 sources has a constant delta equal to its constant modulo -- but 130 of the `up` sites take a RUNTIME delta against a constant modulo, and nothing bounds that delta below the modulo.

Eight columns per lane, all derived before the oracle ran and all confirmed by it at every one of the 256 values. `data` is `lane + 100` and `filling_data` is `lane + 200`, so a data-vs-fill confusion, a lane-index error and a cluster-base error each land on a different number. Columns 0, 1, 6 and 7 are ordinary in-range deltas that pin the model itself, so a disagreement there would have been about the family rather than about the full shift. The dispatch is exactly 32 threads -- one simdgroup -- so no shuffle source is outside the group and every column is defined at every lane.

name: nan-model-loads-stores-and-selects-of-nans
rationale: Whether Metal's data movement keeps a NaN's bits: lane i loads floats a and b and a selector, and stores as float4: a (a float load and store), select(b, a, sel) (an if/else assignment folds to the same select), its neighbour's a through threadgroup memory, and the selected element of float4(b, a, b, a). Lanes: each NaN as a then as b, two distinct NaNs with either selector, and controls. Compiled without fast math unless named; every operand is loaded from a buffer, so nothing folds but what the AIR shows. NaN operands: quiet and signaling of either sign with payloads 0, 1, 2, 0x1000, 0x155555, 0x2aaaaa, 0x3ffffe, 0x3fffff. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

The AIR has no loop.

name: one-simd-group-scatters-four-radix-digits-into-sorted-runs
rationale: Thirty-two lanes, one SIMD group, and four eight-lane digit groups. Each lane ORs its own lane bit into the shared key mask for its digit, then takes the low `lane` bits of that mask and counts them: that popcount is exactly how many earlier lanes share the digit, so it is the lane's rank inside its group. Adding the per-digit base offset (0, 8, 16, 24) sends digit 0 to slots 0-7, digit 1 to 8-15, digit 2 to 16-23 and digit 3 to 24-31, one slot per lane with no collision. Because the digits are laid out in the reverse of that order, the written indices are a permutation that no other reading of the mask or the bit extraction produces: any wrong bit count would either collide two lanes or move a whole run.

name: linked-single-unit-grid-sample-gradient-finish
rationale: A single invocation maps exactly one unit destination coordinate to the sole accumulation-buffer float. The exact linked primary writer stores that finite value into the sole poisoned device-array destination.

name: sum-eight-simdgroup-rows-into-one-byte-per-column
rationale: MLX's transposed bfloat16 GEMV, whose only simdgroup primitive is the three-step air.simd_shuffle_down.u.i16 tree (deltas 16, 8, 4) that folds the eight SM partials of a column onto lane sm=0. in_vec_size=32 makes the tail loop empty and runs the blocked loop exactly once; out_vec_size=marix_ld=8 keeps every one of the 64 threads inside the guard, so the threadgroup barrier and all three shuffles stay convergent and no lane ever shuffles past lane 31. Every in_vec element is 1.0 and each matrix column holds a single power of two 2^(k/4) at k%4==0, gated by a per-column mask, so column c reduces to exactly mask[c] = 1, 16, 4, 2, 128, 255, 170, 85 -- eight distinct bytes that pin the lane-to-(sm,column) mapping and each shuffle delta separately. Every partial sum is a sum of distinct powers of two below 256, so each bfloat fmuladd and add is exact and the answer is independent of accumulation order.
